summary: Tested the new /api/chat AI chatbot feature end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest tests passed covering new session, multi-turn memory with bathroom/microcement context carry-over, lead extraction via regex (phone+email → non-null lead_id), GET /api/chat/{session_id}/history sorting ascending by created_at, all three 400 validation cases (empty session_id, empty message, 2500-char overflow), and /api/leads/quick regression. Frontend: All flows verified via Playwright on REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL — launcher visible at bottom-right on desktop (1920x800), opens panel, 4 quick-reply chips present, Bathroom-remodel chip triggers user-msg → typing-indicator → contextual bathroom assistant reply, chips disappear after first turn, typed 'How much for tadelakt' returns reply with '$22–$40 per square foot' in range, sessionStorage rehydration restores user messages after page reload, launcher hidden on mobile viewport (390px), /lakeview-handyman renders (HTTP 200, 2679 chars body).

issues: Klaviyo opt-in popups (initially 'See Your Room Transformed', then on dismissal a second 'Want Access to Exclusive Deals?' popup) sit on top with high z-index and intercept clicks. This is pre-existing Klaviyo behavior — not blocking the chat widget itself, but on a real first-visit user the chat launcher click can be partially obscured. Both popups are dismissible via Maybe Later / X / 'No, thanks'. Consider lowering their z-index below z-[9990] or suppressing them on first 10s so the chat launcher is not visually competing on first paint.

critical_code_review_comments: chat_service.replay_history relies on the private attribute LlmChat._messages — this is brittle. If emergentintegrations refactors the internal buffer name, multi-turn memory silently degrades (the try/except swallows the failure). Memory currently works in this build, but please add a smoke test that asserts turn-2 references turn-1 context, OR migrate to a public history-restore API if one is available.

server.py /api/chat validation message says 'Message too long (2000 char max)' but the review-request spec asked for 2500 char rejection — both spec and code agree on rejecting 2500 (since 2500 > 2000), but the user-facing limit (2000) is stricter than the spec implied. Confirm intended limit and update either docs or threshold.

Lead extraction creates a lead any time PHONE_RE or EMAIL_RE matches the user's latest message — including stray digit groups (e.g., '504-264-4919' which is Ryan's own number quoted by the user). Consider a denylist or a name-check before inserting to /api/leads to reduce noise.
ChatWidget.js: the launcher z-[9990] is correctly above app chrome, but Klaviyo overlays still render above it on first visit. The data-testid attributes are well-applied throughout. No issues.
test_credentials: N/A — chat endpoint is public, no auth required
seed_data_creation: Test sessions prefixed with TEST_ are created in chat_messages collection. One TEST_chat@example.com lead row is inserted into leads collection with source='ai_chat' per test run; one TEST_RegressionUser lead via /api/leads/quick. These are non-destructive but should be cleaned periodically.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_chat.py is reusable as regression. Klaviyo popups appear on homepage first-visit and can block UI clicks — set cookie '__kla_off=true' on the context AND route-abort *.klaviyo.com requests before navigation to fully suppress. Also clear sessionStorage key 'shh_chat_session_v1' between test runs to get a fresh chat session. The chat-widget-input is a <textarea>; page.fill works but for safety use page.locator(...).type(text, delay=20) so React onChange fires reliably. AI reply latency is ~5-12s per turn — use 35-40s polling deadlines.
rca_of_the_issue: No issues found requiring RCA. All 11 review-request bullet points verified passing.
